method.value: Select NUV-r-J star-forming galaxies at 4<z<5 from FARMER COSMOS2020, M*>10^9.5, remove AGN, cross-match with A3COSMOS coverage (PB>0.2)

evidence.quote: This reduces our sample to 440 galaxies
($m_{\rm IRAC3.6}<26\,$AB and $\chi^{2}_{\rm reduced} < 10$) and accurate photometric redshifts ($\Delta z/(1+z) <0.1$)

validation.value: KS test shows ALMA-covered sample is indistinguishable from the parent sample

evidence.quote: distributions that are indistinguishable (Kolmogorov-Smirnov test) from those of their parent sample of 5,810 galaxies

analysis_steps.goal: Stack ALMA visibilities in uv domain

method.value: Rescale visibility amplitudes to rest-frame 150 um luminosity with SED template, shift phase centres to galaxy positions, concat per stellar mass bin, tclean, read central pixel

evidence.quote: Finally, we measured the stacked $L_{\rm 150}^{\rm rest}$ (i.e., $\langle L_{\rm 150}^{\rm rest}\rangle$) using the central pixel value

key_parameters.value: SED template of Bethermin et al. 2017; gencal and applycal; three mass bins

evidence.quote: by using the redshift of the source, the SED template of (cite: Bethermin.2017) and the CASA tasks `gencal` and `applycal`
using instead 2D Gaussian fits at the phase center of the stacked images gave consistent $\langle L_{\rm 150}^{\rm rest}\rangle$ measurements
we made 100 realizations of the stacking analysis, using for each realization a different sample, drawn from the original one

method.value: Linear conversions from L150 to L_IR and then SFR_IR

evidence.quote: \frac{\langle{\rm SFR}_{\rm IR}\rangle}{M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}}} = 1\times10^{-10}\times\frac{\langle L_{\rm IR}\rangle}{L_\odot}

assumptions.value: Chabrier IMF; conversion corresponds approximately to modified blackbody with T_dust=41 K

evidence.quote: It corresponds approximately to that of a modified blackbody function with a dust temperature of 41 K

validation.value: Template within 5% of the conversion factor

evidence.quote: it yields a $L_{\rm IR}$-to-$L_{\rm 150}^{\rm rest}$ conversion factor that is within 5% to that of Eq.

method.value: Take L_UV (1600 A) from best-fit LePhare SEDs, compute beta_UV from 1600 and 2300 A, weighted by visibility numbers, bootstrap errors; SFR_UV = 1.5e-10 L_UV

evidence.quote: we used their rest-frame luminosities at $1600\,\r{A}$ and $2300\,\r{A}$
assuming the (cite: Bruzual.2003) model with a delayed star formation history

method.value: Compare stack points with Meurer/Overzier relations; linear fit of log IRX vs log M*; fit MS normalization of Schreiber 2015

method.value: Multiply and integrate the fiducial SMF with MS and IRX–M* relations; Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation; total SFRD integrated down to 0.03 M*

evidence.quote: by multiplying and then integrating our fiducial SMF with our fiducial MS

evidence.quote: MS$_{\rm fid.}\equiv\,{\rm MS}_{\rm S15}-0.15\,$dex

assumptions.value: All SFGs at a given mass lie on the MS (no starburst contribution)

evidence.quote: by construction we have assumed that at a given mass, all SFGs are MS galaxies

fitting.value: Schechter plus power law fit to Weaver et al. 2023 SMF points at 3.5<z<4.5 and 4.5<z<5.5

evidence.quote: with the combination of a Schechter function dominating at low stellar masses and a power-law dominating at high stellar masses

validation.value: Repeated with Schechter SMF and with JWST SMF of Weibel et al. 2024

evidence.quote: we also tested the robustness of our calculations against the most recent JWST-derived SMF from (cite: Weibel.2024)

results_numeric.value: 5810 parent; 440 with ALMA coverage; 64 primary targets

evidence.quote: Of these 440 galaxies, 64 can be considered as the primary target of a given ALMA observation

findings_qualitative.value: IRX–beta_UV at z~4.5 is consistent with local starbursts (Meurer), disfavoring SMC-like flatter relation

evidence.quote: This distribution is overall very consistent with the local reference for starbursts from (cite: Meurer.1999)

findings_qualitative.value: Cosmic SFRD is dominated by SFGs with M* of 10^9.5-10.5 Msun

evidence.quote: The cosmic SFRD at $z\sim4.5$ is dominated by SFGs with a stellar mass of $10^{9.5-10.5}\,M_\odot$.

claims.hypothesis: Does the IRX–beta_UV relation at z~4.5 differ from local starbursts?
claims.experiment: Stack ALMA uv data of mass-complete SFGs in 3 mass bins and compare IRX and beta_UV with local relations
claims.result: Points consistent with Meurer/Overzier; flatter SMC relation disfavored
claims.finding: Dust grain properties similar to local starbursts

evidence.quote: our measurements disfavor a flatter IRX–$\beta_{\rm UV}$ relation, such as that observed in the Small Magellanic Cloud

claims.experiment: Linear fit to IRX versus M* from stacks, compare to Pannella 2015
claims.result: Slope 1.1 to 1.8; ~-0.5 dex in IRX at 10^9.75

evidence.quote: Our measurements favor a slight steepening of the IRX–$M_\ast$ relation at $z\sim4.5$

claims.hypothesis: How much of the cosmic SFRD is dust attenuated at z~4.5?
claims.experiment: Integrate SMF x MS x IRX–M*

evidence.quote: the fraction of the cosmic SFRD that is attenuated by dust remains significant ($\sim68\pm10\%$) even at such an early cosmic epoch

why_this_data.value: Bands 6 and 7 are close to dust emission peak of z~4.5 SFGs; A3COSMOS gives homogeneous archival data

evidence.quote: they are close to the peak of the dust emission of $z\sim4.5$ SFGs and therefore provide good proxies of their infrared luminosities

why_this_method.value: uv-domain stacking handles heterogeneous resolution; individual galaxies are mostly undetected

evidence.quote: even though most of these galaxies are not detected individually in the ALMA archival data

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photometric L_UV and beta_UV instead of SED-based; Schechter SMF and Weibel JWST SMF instead of the fiducial; both gave qualitatively unchanged results

evidence.quote: Using a Schechter SMF instead of our fiducial SMF would not qualitatively change any of these results

limitations_admitted.value: Sample may miss optically-dark heavily attenuated galaxies; ALMA primary targets bias the MS normalization

evidence.quote: this sample may still miss part of the population of optically-dark galaxies that are heavily dust attenuated

referee_caveats_inferred: Mean IR luminosity depends on a single assumed SED template and conversion (41 K-like)
